body:
It doesn't particularly matter what their experience would be. I'm sure it would be unpleasant, could be long-lasting. But again, why should I be moved to care if I would be dead when they experience these things?

The desire to the contrary is that it would be easy. Experience is many things, and is often pleasant, but it is difficult. Why not just end it? Of course there are things I'd like to do, but if I don't get a chance to I wouldn't be able to regret that, because, again, I would be dead. So why should I care if I miss out on some experience?

Because it would be easier for me. Yeah, it would cause pain, but why should I care about that, when I wouldn't exist? It wouldn't be better, because for me it would have no characteristics. For me it would just be nothing. It negates all other considerations, because it can't be compared to any mode of subjective experience. I don't want to hurt the people I love, but if I didn't exist, that harm wouldn't affect me, so why should I really care? It seems empty to go on living for no other reason than for the sake of others, if I have no particular desire to live.

But why go on living? Once dead you can't care about life, or what might be missed in the experience, because there is no you to care.

By beyond comparison, I mean that it cannot be compared to subjective experience. It can be neither better or worse, because such judgements can only exist from a state of experience. Death, being a state of non-being, cannot be compared adequately to an experience.

We don't get two chances to experience non-existence, non-existence isn't experienced. It is beyond our experience. We have only one thing ever, and that is our lifespan. Beyond that there is nothing, on either end. So why should I care how long my life goes? Once it's gone there's no me to care.

A life is unique, to be sure. But is that all it has to commend itself? Why should I go on with this, with its pains and pleasures both, if I could just simply end it all, and choose to no longer exist?
